title: CreativeInstruct: Teaching LLMs to Balance Quality and Creativity Without Losing Diversity
description: New instruction-tuning method teaches LLMs to inject special [StartCreativity] spans, matching multi-model diversity without sacrificing quality. Beats post-trained LLMs in human creativity evaluations 70% of the time. GRPO applied to CreativeInstruct improves ~4% on AMC and ~5% points on MATH. Introduces a structural diversity metric based on graph edit distance.

title: Against Explainable AI in Law: Why Justifiable AI Matters for Credit Scoring
description: Argues against narrow 'right to explanation' interpretations for AI in credit scoring. Proposes that legal justification, not just technical explanations, is the only way to safeguard creditor rights under EU law. Integrates EU legal framework with technical ML analysis.

title: AI Restaurant Recommendations: 85.6% of Venues Never Recommended by Any System
description: First census-denominated audit of AI venue recommendations across 4,776 cafes/restaurants/bars in Bali. Evaluates ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity against complete market data. Key finding: review volume, not star rating, drives visibility. 93 recommendations of permanently closed venues — staleness, not hallucination, is the practical failure mode.

title: LLM Agentic Framework Plans Chemical Syntheses Rivaling Human Chemists
description: SynthEx, an LLM-based agentic framework, plans routes to complex natural products beyond reach of conventional design algorithms. Proposes competing strategies, self-critiques designs, expert chemists judged its key steps comparable to published human syntheses. Releases 1000+ routes as open SynthAtlas database.

title: SkillProx: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Proximal Textual Gradient Descent
description: New framework for LLM agent skills that couples closed-loop diagnostic evolution with utility-aware proximal refinement. Estimates individual skill contributions using frozen leave-one-out utility audit. Applies validation-gated consolidation, demotion, or removal. Improves average accuracy by 3.0 percentage points over gradient-based baseline.
